claims.claim: Origen of Alexandria, son of the martyr Leonides, was born around 184/185 in Alexandria and died around 253/54 in Tyre.
He served as head of the Catechetical School of Alexandria under Bishop Demetrius.
Origen wrote them to fulfill his chief aim of interpreting Scripture and to draw out its allegorical significance.
The Homilies on Exodus survive only in a Latin translation made by Rufinus of Aquileia, with only fragmentary Greek portions remaining.
Modern editions are based on the Rufinus Latin manuscript tradition, which has been edited and translated into English in the 20th and 21st centuries.
